neighbours.label: 'keep / kept / keeps' in the sense of holding something steady (kept pace, keeps the same axis, keep your password): the other side of the − pole, which fires on ' change'
fire: Salaries have barely kept up with rising rents.
Always keep your passport in a secure pocket.
The thermos keeps the soup warm until lunch.
The newsletter will keep members informed about events.
Despite the wind, the runner kept a steady rhythm.
A flywheel keeps the same speed under varying load.
Please keep this code secret from other users.
The museum has kept the room exactly as it was.
quiet: Salaries have barely grown despite rising rents.
Always show your passport at the border desk.
The thermos holds a litre of soup for lunch.
The newsletter will reach members before the events.
Despite the wind, the runner finished the race.
A flywheel stores energy under varying load.
Please enter this code when the screen asks.
The museum has opened the room to visitors.

notes: The label does not cover everything: 'turned the corner' scored 0.89 and 'turned the page' 0.34 in probes, peaking on ' the' / ' turned', so the pole also fires on some 'turned the X' phrases that are not 'keep'.
